summary: Eugène Burnouf was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He worked at the Court of Appeal of Paris, the Société Asiatique, and as a teacher at the Collège de France (1832–1852).

Eugène Denis specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning his Ph.D. at the University of Paris by 1976. He served as a research scholar at the CNRS (1961–1986) and held posts at Bangkok University and Chulalongkorn University (1976).

Eugène Henri Guillaume Edgard Monseur was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Charles Michel at the University of Liège. He founded the Société du folklore wallon in 1889 and served as Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Grammar at Université libre de Bruxelles (1888–1912).

Eugène Jacquet was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Sinology. He attended Lycée Louis-le-Grand and studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat, Antoine-Léonard Chézy, Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, Pierre-Amédée Jaubert, and Eugène Burnouf.

Eugène Obermiller was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (Theodore Stcherbatsky) and Dondub Buddhayin. He held positions at the Institute of Buddhist Culture, University of Chicago, and Institute of Oriental Studies.
Eugène Pittard was a scholar in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at the University of Geneva from circa 1894 to 1899 and later held a post there from circa 1916 to 1949.

Eugène Tisserant was a scholar of history, archaeology, and religious studies. He completed his education at Lycée Notre-Dame Saint-Sigisbert, the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales, and the École du Louvre.

Eugène-Armand Hauvette-Besnault was an Indologist who studied at the Petit Séminaire de Saint-Nicolas-du-Chardonnet and under Eugène Burnouf. He held posts as librarian at the École Normale Supérieure (ca. 1864–1890), Sanskrit teacher at the Sorbonne (1868), and at the EPHE (ca. 1868–1890).
Eugénie Bazin-Foucher was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She completed her studies at the Sorbonne and at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1915–1918) under Sylvain Lévi.

Eugénie Sellers was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at Girton College, Cambridge, and the British School at Athens. She later held positions at Chatsworth House (1904–1908) and the British School at Rome (1909–1925).

Eun Hino is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a master's course at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo as a project researcher (ca. 2011–2015) and at Musashino University as assistant professor and associate professor.
Eun Maeda was a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as president (学長) of both Toyo University and Ryukoku University.

Eun-su Cho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed her Ph.D. under Padmanabh S. Jaini at the University of California, Berkeley. She taught at the University of Michigan until 2004 and became professor of Buddhist Philosophy at Seoul National University.
Eunyoung Choe is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Korea University. She served as an HK professor at Geumgang University, attested between 2013 and 2015.

Eustaquio Echauri Martínez was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Conciliar Seminary of Pamplona and Universidad Central. He held professorships in Latin at the University of Barcelona (1920) and in Greek and Sanskrit at Complutense University of Madrid (1940).
Eva De Clercq is an Indology scholar who earned her PhD at Ghent University (1999–2003) and became a permanent member there in 2025.

Eva K. Neumaier is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Attested in 2006, she was Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Calgary, as well as Professor Emeritus, former Chair, and Professor of East Asian Studies at the University of Alberta.
Eva K. Neumaier-Dargyay is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Rigzin. She held a post attested in 1992 at the University of Calgary.

Eva Tichy is a linguist and Indologist who studied under Karl Hoffmann at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg and completed her habilitation at the University of Marburg. She held the chair of Indo-European Studies at the University of Freiburg from 1993 to 2017.

Eva Wilden is an Indologist who completed her M.A., doctorate, and habilitation at the University of Hamburg. She held a post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (2003) and was appointed Professor at the University of Hamburg in 2017.
